description: standard_flags:manifest:check and a client's contract check share these semantics. Each case gives the committed manifest (the baseline the client was built against) and the current one, and today's date (UTC). `stale`: the two documents differ as JSON values (the server task also compares the file's bytes). `removed_wires`: every wire (audience + name) the committed manifest tells an audience, from a flag's audiences or a tombstone's serve block still served today (today <= until), that the current manifest neither exposes to that audience nor serves from a tombstone whose until is today or later. `type_changes`: every wire both manifests tell the same audience whose JSON type (a flag's type; a static wire's boolean or string value) differs. Both lists are sorted by audience, then wire. `status` is breaking when either list is non-empty, else stale when stale, else ok. Version 1 manifests are server-only.

cases.name: a changed default is only stale
an added wire and an added flag are only stale
a min_client added to a flag is only stale
a dropped alias with no tombstone is a removed wire
a removed flag whose tombstone serves every wire is only stale
a removed flag whose tombstone serves only some wires
a deprecated wire dropped before its until date is a removed wire; one past it may go
until is inclusive: on the until date the wire is still owed
the day after until, the deprecated wire may go
a tombstone that stopped serving a wire doesn't cover it
a wire whose flag became a different kind changed type
a deprecated wire that now serves a string changed type
a wire moved to another flag of the same type is only stale
a wire moved to another audience is removed from the first
an audience made public is only stale
removed wires and type changes are reported together
a version 1 committed manifest is read: stale, and its wires still checked
